subject: B1D5DEBD4BDBE604BF563353CF2199E1
introduction: These hundred readings, most of them from letters and prayers of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, ask one thing in many ways: be a lamp. Be a father to the orphan and a guide to the erring; let the candle of the heart never go out; be the cause of the illumination of others, in your family, your town and the world. Beside them stand the sayings they echo, on a city set on a hill, a candle on a candlestick, the wise who shine as the stars, a prophet as a lamp that gives light. Other passages keep the image honest: alms done to be seen, the mote and the beam, Paul's question to the confident guide of the blind, John the Baptist who was not the Light but its witness, the Buddha's counsel to be lamps unto yourselves, and Milton, blind, on those who only stand and wait.
questions: The readings ask each person to be a lamp. Who has been one for you, and what exactly did they do?
Jesus says both let your light shine before men and do not your alms to be seen. How do you hold those two sayings together in practice?
Paul warns the person who is confident of being a guide to the blind. What keeps the wish to guide others from becoming self-regard?
John the Baptist is called a witness to the Light and not the Light. What difference does that distinction make to how one tries to help another person?
Several readings speak of guiding one's own relatives by love and example. Why is that so hard, and what have you seen work?
George Eliot and Milton speak of hidden lives and of those who only stand and wait. What light can a person give who is unseen or unable to do much?

outside.why: Job says of his better days: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame; I was a father to the poor.
In the parable ten virgins took their lamps to meet the bridegroom, and five were wise and five were foolish.
William Blake wrote that we are put on earth a little space that we may learn to bear the beams of love.
Jesus sent out his disciples with the words: freely ye have received, freely give.
Shakespeare's Portia, coming home at night, says: how far that little candle throws his beams! So shines a good deed in a naughty world.
Jesus said: let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father.
In the same sermon Jesus said: take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them. How can a person be a shining lamp and not do good in order to be seen?
Jesus told of a man who made a great supper and bade many, and they all with one consent began to make excuse.
The psalm says: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
Isaiah says that the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
The psalmist prays: O send out Thy light and Thy truth; let them lead me.
The Qur’an says that God is the protecting guardian of those who believe; He bringeth them out of darkness into light.
Jesus said: walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you.
The Qur’an says that there is no compulsion in religion, since the right direction is distinct from error. What is owed to those who are shown a path and turn aside from it?
Zacharias sings of the dayspring from on high, come to give light to them that sit in darkness and to guide our feet into the way of peace.

Jesus asked whether those on whom the tower in Siloam fell were sinners above all others, and answered: I tell you, nay. How should people who believe themselves guided speak of those they think are not?
John's Gospel says that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light.
Proverbs says that the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he that winneth souls is wise.
The Qur’an describes its Prophet as a summoner unto God by His permission, and as a lamp that giveth light.
John's Gospel says of John the Baptist: he was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. What is the difference between being a lamp and being the light it carries?
Proverbs says that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
The psalm calls the word of God a lamp unto the feet and a light unto the path.
Jesus said that men do not light a candle and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick, and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.
Jesus said: blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Paul says that we, beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image.
Jesus asked why one beholds the mote in a brother's eye and considers not the beam in one's own. What has to happen in a person before they try to make other hearts clean?
When Moses came down from the mountain he did not know that the skin of his face shone.
George Herbert wrote that a servant who works as for God makes drudgery divine.
The Buddha's last counsel to Ananda was: be ye lamps unto yourselves; betake yourselves to no external refuge. Is light something each person must find alone, or something passed from one to another?
The Light Verse of the Qur’an ends: light upon light; God guideth unto His light whom He will.
The Book of Daniel says that they that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever.
The psalmist says to God: in Thy light shall we see light.
Paul says: I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord.
The Letter to the Ephesians says: ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord; walk as children of light.
The psalm says that he that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
The psalmist prays: create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
Jesus said: I am come to send fire on the earth, and what will I, if it be already kindled?
David sings: Thou art my lamp, O Lord, and the Lord will lighten my darkness.
The first letter of Peter speaks of a people called out of darkness into His marvellous light, to show forth His praises.
Milton, considering how his light was spent in blindness, concluded that they also serve who only stand and wait. What forms of light are there for someone who cannot be a brilliant lamp?
Plato held that education does not put sight into the soul but turns the whole soul toward the light.
The second letter to Timothy says that the servant of the Lord must not strive, but be gentle unto all, in meekness instructing.
Jesus said that they that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
Through Isaiah God says: I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not; I will make darkness light before them.
Jesus expected to be told the proverb: physician, heal thyself. What must a teacher who adapts the remedy to each patient have done about their own condition?

Paul asks one who is confident of being a guide of the blind and a light of them in darkness: thou which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? What are the dangers of thinking of oneself as a source of light to others?
Paul asks the Romans to rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.
Isaiah hears the promise: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground.
The psalm says: he leadeth me beside the still waters; he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness.
Jesus spoke at the well of a water that becomes in the one who drinks it a well springing up.
The Qur’an says to its Prophet: We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples.
James warns: be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation. What responsibility comes with setting out to guide others?
Paul recalls words of Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive.
Proverbs says that a merry heart doeth good like a medicine, but a broken spirit drieth the bones.
Jeremiah asks: is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there?
The first letter of Peter hopes that those who obey not the word may without the word be won by the conduct of those closest to them.
The Letter to Titus says: in all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works.
Jesus said that no prophet is accepted in his own country. Why is one's own family often the hardest place to be a light, and what works there?
Peter said: of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons.
The elder writes: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
Jesus said of John the Baptist: he was a burning and a shining light.
Jesus likened the kingdom of heaven to leaven hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
Thomas à Kempis says that love is a great thing, which makes every heavy thing light.
Jesus told his followers to pray in secret, and not as the hypocrites, who love to be seen of men. When should spiritual grace be displayed in the marketplace, and when kept out of sight?
Isaiah calls: arise, shine, for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
Shelley's traveller found a shattered statue in the desert whose pedestal still read: look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair.
At Sinai Moses saw a bush that burned with fire and was not consumed.
In the Qur’an Moses is told to thrust his hand within his armpit: it will come forth white without hurt, another token.
The crowd at Pentecost said of the disciples: these men are full of new wine.
Jesus said that no man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place.
Paul says that though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
Paul asks the Thessalonians to rejoice evermore, pray without ceasing, and in every thing give thanks.
Isaiah promises one who draws out his soul to the hungry: then shall thy light rise in obscurity.
Proverbs says: trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding.
At Pentecost there appeared cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
George Eliot wrote that the growing good of the world is partly dependent on unhistoric acts and on those who lived faithfully a hidden life. Must holy souls be seen to change a place?
Jesus said that the harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.
Paul says that eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, the things which God hath prepared.
Paul hopes that his friends will shine as lights in the world.
Jesus said: woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you. What is the danger in being pointed out and admired?
Jesus told his followers: ye are the light of the world; a city that is set on a hill cannot be hid.
Paul tells the Thessalonians: ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day.
Proverbs says that heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop, but a good word maketh it glad.
John's Gospel speaks of the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.
Jesus said that where two or three are gathered together in his name, he is in the midst of them.
Paul asks Timothy to be an example in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
The Letter to the Colossians says: set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
Emerson asked each person to watch that gleam of light which flashes across the mind from within.
Macbeth says: out, out, brief candle; life's but a walking shadow. What answers the feeling that a life is too short and small to light anything?
Hopkins wrote that the world is charged with the grandeur of God; it will flame out, like shining from shook foil.
Dante begins his Paradise: the glory of Him who moveth everything doth penetrate the universe, and shine in one part more and in another less.
Job remembers the days when God's candle shined upon his head, and by His light he walked through darkness.
The Letter to the Ephesians quotes: awake thou that sleepest, and Christ shall give thee light.
The elder brother in the parable had always been faithful, and was angry when the lost one was welcomed. What temptation comes to those who think of themselves as awake while others sleep?
Isaiah hears: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles.
The master in the parable says: well done, thou good and faithful servant.
The psalmist says: the entrance of Thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.
Isaiah says that the sun shall be no more thy light by day, but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light.
Milton, blind, begins a book of his poem: hail, holy Light, offspring of Heaven firstborn.
The Qur’an speaks of a day when the earth shineth with the light of her Lord.

romans-guide-of-the-blind.text: And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness, An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law. Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself

peter-won-by-the-conversation.text: that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear

psalm-send-out-thy-light.text: O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me; let them bring me unto thy holy hill, and to thy tabernacles

isaiah-blind-by-a-way-they-knew-not.text: And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not; I will lead them in paths that they have not known: I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight. These things will I do unto them, and not forsake them

matthew-candle-under-a-bushel.text: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house

thessalonians-children-of-light.text: Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness

samuel-thou-art-my-lamp.text: For thou art my lamp, O Lord: and the Lord will lighten my darkness

job-candle-shined-upon-my-head.text: Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me; When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness

luke-lighted-a-candle.text: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, neither under a bushel, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light. The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light

psalm-he-leadeth-me.text: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake

quran-white-hand.text: And thrust thy hand within thine armpit, it will come forth white without hurt. (That will be) another token.

quran-light-upon-light.text: Light upon light. Allah guideth unto His light whom He will

titus-pattern-of-good-works.text: In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you
